title: Third Conditional: Rules and Examples — Quiz 82A
content:
## Third Conditional: Rules and Examples

Use the past perfect in the if clause and would have with the past participle in the main clause.

### Lesson focus

1. If you had asked me, I would have helped you.
2. The situation refers to a past condition and result that did not happen.

### Understand the pattern

A third conditional separates an unreal past condition from its imagined consequence. In the if-clause, use past perfect; in the result, use would have + past participle. Do not put would have into both clauses in the standard classroom pattern.

### Worked answers and explanation

If you had asked me, I would have helped you means you did not ask, so the imagined help did not occur. Reversing the clauses is possible: 'I would have helped you if you had asked me'. A comma is usual after an opening if-clause but normally unnecessary when it comes second.

### Try another

Correct: If she would have called, I would have answered.

### Suggested answer

If she had called, I would have answered. Had called supplies the unreal past condition, while would have answered gives its imagined result.
